Team —

Finance is finalizing the Q3 forecast and we need a quick certification pass on all open opportunities slated for Q3 close. I ran a small export (attached) and flagged deals where stage or close date look inconsistent with our commit criteria. Please action the items below by EOD Friday (2026-07-02):

- Confirm stage mapping: set to "Commit" only if there is a firm PO, signed SOW, or an explicit procurement timeline.
- If the deal is only a verbal/soft-commit, mark stage "Verbal" and set close date to the realistic quarter (do not force into Q3).
- Attach at least one piece of evidence to the opportunity (calendar invite, signed SOW, PO, or a confirmation email).
- If you cannot provide evidence, change close date out of Q3 or move to "At Risk" and add a short note.

Attached: sfdc_closeproof_export_0626.csv (report: opportunities closing in Q3 lacking evidence).

I will pull a second pass on Monday and roll final numbers to finance. If anything needs escalation (contracting, billing terms, procurement redlines), loop Ben in.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Rishi — good question. Short guidance from Sales Ops (apply to all reps):

- Move to "Commit" only when there is demonstrable commercial proof: signed SOW, executed PO, or an email thread from a procurement stakeholder confirming a PO number and expected issue date.
- If the buyer has given a firm verbal but procurement hasn't provided dates/correspondence, leave as "Verbal" and add a one-line note summarizing the vendor contact + date of verbal.
- For large deals (>$250k ARR) where procurement has committed verbally and legal has reviewed, please cc Ben and attach any legal intake notes — we will treat these as soft-commits but Finance should get a follow-up before finaling the forecast.

Also — for Stanley Health (D-98732) specifically: Brett told us on 6/24 they would sign a revised SOW and send the PO by 6/30. If you have the signed doc, attach it; if not, leave as "Verbal" and set close date to 2026-07-15 unless you have reason to shorten.
